Deze leden vernemen graag of het waar is dat de richtlijn in die landen niet apart wordt geïmplementeerd.
Asks about effectiveness of marking against criminal use, the status of existing permits and unmarked firearms, and whether the directive needs tightening.
Does the government share the view that the biggest problem concerns the use of illegal weapons that by their nature will not be registered and perhaps not marked either?
Deelt de regering de mening dat het grootste probleem het gebruik van illegale wapens betreft die uit de aard der zaak niet geregistreerd zullen worden en wellicht ook niet gemarkeerd zullen zijn?
Asks why the 20-year retention period was chosen, why destruction records are not registered, and how the rules fit existing exemptions and airsoft commitments.
Why are these data not kept until the weapon in question is destroyed, or at least until it is rendered unusable?
Waarom worden deze gegevens niet bewaard tot het moment dat het betreffende wapen is vernietigd of in ieder geval tot het moment dat zij onbruikbaar worden gemaakt?
Asks whether marking actually improves enforcement and inspection of legal firearms, whether police capacity suffices for annual checks, and whether collectors' interests are considered.
Does the Special Laws Bureau, responsible for these checks at the police, have sufficient capacity to check everyone as often as prescribed?
Heeft het Bureau bijzondere wetten, dat bij de politie verantwoordelijk voor deze controles, voldoende capaciteit om iedereen zo vaak te controleren als wordt voorgeschreven?
Asks for an estimate of the implementation costs for government organisations such as the police and defence.
They would welcome an estimate of the size of these burdens for government organisations that must implement this directive, such as the police and defence.
Gaarne ontvangen zij een schatting van de omvang van deze lasten voor overheidsorganisaties die deze richtlijn moeten implementeren, zoals de politieorganisatie en defensie.
Asks whether weapons already in the Verona registration system need physical marking and whether checks can rely on registry data, raising verification and administrative oversight questions.
Can the government confirm that the national licensing module system Verona (hereafter: Verona) stores all data on firearms registered in the Netherlands, including the country of origin?

Kan de regering bevestigen dat in het landelijk vergunningen modulesysteem Verona (hierna: Verona) alle gegevens zijn opgeslagen van de in Nederland geregistreerde vuurwapens, inclusief het land van herkomst?
Doubts that enforcement of the marking duty can work without extra police capacity or funding and asks how the EU will ensure member states control acquisition and possession of weapons.
These members do not yet clearly see how enforcement and control of the marking obligation will work.
Deze leden zien echter nog niet goed voor zich hoe de handhaving en controle van de markeringsplicht eruit gaat zien.
Has no further questions and endorses the third amendment clarifying exemptions for armed forces, police and collectors.
The bill and the accompanying amendments give these members no reason to ask further questions.
Het wetsvoorstel en bijhorende voorstellen tot wijziging geven deze leden geen aanleiding tot het stellen van nadere vragen.
Asks what 'placed on the market' means, whether marking applies to private sales, and whether police staffing shortages can absorb the extra work and whether budget will be provided.
To what extent does this marking obligation bring additional work for the police, also viewed from the investigative possibilities?
In hoeverre brengt deze markeringsplicht extra werkzaamheden met zich mee voor de politie, overigens ook bezien vanuit de opsporingsmogelijkheden?

v.summary: The Raad van State advised on the bill implementing EU Directive 2008/51 on firearms control, supporting its aim but raising objections on the penalty for breaching the marking obligation, the broad delegation clause for arms brokers, terminology, and late implementation. The government's reply accepted most points: it added a reference to penalties in article 55, dropped the delegation clause and related definition, and aligned terminology, while deferring penalties for falsifying markings to a separate bill.
concerns: The broad delegation for regulating arms brokers's activities insufficiently justified and undermined the primacy of the legislature; the government dropped the delegation clause.
Penalties for breaching the marking obligation were missing from articles 54-56; article 55 was supplemented, but penalties for falsifying or removing markings were deferred to a separate bill.
Terminology and definitions should align with the Directive; the arms-broker definition was removed and the firearm definition was aligned, with a redactional note on the heading adopted.
The explanatory memorandum should address consequences of exceeding the implementation deadline; the advice was adopted.

32811.s: The bill amends the Dutch Maritime Transport Act to repeal article 8, which underpinned ministerial rules on dispute settlement for liner conference membership, and to repeal article 32, which contained enforcement rules for conference-related recommendations. It also rewords article 20(2)(c) so that compliance with foreign-state measures implementing international maritime agreements is a ground covered by the Act, aligning the law with EU regulations 1419/2006 and 1490/2007.
32811.j: The memorandum justifies repealing article 8 because the minister's intervention powers must fit within the framework of the TFEU, and repealing article 32 follows from article 8's repeal since the enforcement rules relate to the same conference procedure.
q: For that reason this article is repealed.
Om die reden wordt dit artikel ingetrokken.
p: Repealing article 8 removes the statutory basis for ministerial rules on settling disputes over liner conference membership, reducing a dispute-resolution mechanism available to shipping parties.
Repealing article 32 removes the rules on enforcing binding recommendations from the conference dispute procedure, which could weaken parties' enforcement routes before national courts.
Artikel I, onderdeel B (artikel 20, tweede lid, onderdeel c)
The reworded ground allows the minister to act on compliance with foreign-state measures implementing international maritime agreements, broadening the basis for intervention in shipping.

parties: The SP asks the government to explain the consequences of denouncing the UN Liner Code for developing countries' cargo rights, trade, costs and revenues, and whether they were consulted.
Can the government explain what denouncing the Convention on a Code of Conduct for Liner Conferences for developing countries means?
Kan de regering toelichten wat het opzeggen van het Verdrag inzake een gedragscode voor lijnvaartconferences voor ontwikkelingslanden betekent?

v.summary: The Raad van State advised on a bill repealing the group exemption for liner shipping conferences in the Wet vervoer over zee, noting that the explanatory memorandum did not address whether EU competition rules apply to the UN Code's dispute settlement and that pending disputes could arise without transitional provisions. The government's reply explained that the Code has no transitional regime, that no Dutch disputes are known, and amended the bill so that repeal of article 32 enters into force by royal decree on the date the denunciation of the Code takes effect.
concerns: The Afdeling argued that pending or future disputes under the Code's arbitration procedure could still arise and that the bill lacks retroactivity or a transitional provision for them, so the explanatory memorandum should be revised and the bill supplemented if necessary.

The Afdeling advised that the explanatory memorandum be adapted in light of the observation on applicability of competition rules and pending disputes, and the government amended article I, part C and its explanatory memorandum accordingly.

33027.s: The bill approves the 2010 EU–Republic of Korea free trade agreement for the European part of the Netherlands, as required under Article 91(1) of the Constitution. It enters into force the day after publication in the Staatsblad, and the explanatory memorandum sets out which parts of the agreement fall under national competence.
33027.j: The memorandum justifies the approval by noting that the agreement has a mixed character, so Member States retain competence over some subjects, and that later technical amendments to annexes covering those subjects extend to the approval.
q: Approval of the Free Trade Agreement means that for these subjects, later amendments to the annexes concerning these subjects that are technical in nature also extend to those amendments.

Goedkeuring van het Vrijhandelsakkoord betekent dat voor deze onderwerpen latere wijzigingen van de bijlagen die betrekking hebben op deze onderwerpen en uitvoeringstechnisch van aard zijn, zich ook uitstrekt tot de deze wijzigingen.

parties: Asks about the delay between initialling and signing, the deferral of the Kaesong zone status to a working group, and the timing of tariff abolition.
The PvdA members ask why the status of the North Korean Kaesong industrial zone was not settled at once but deferred to a working group.
De leden van de PvdA-fractie vragen waarom de status van de Noord-Koreaanse industriezone Kaesong niet in één keer geregeld is, maar wordt doorgeschoven naar een werkgroep.
Asks about the effects of the agreement on the competitiveness of Dutch firms and on Dutch import and export with South Korea.
Both the PvdA and CDA members ask what the free trade agreement means for the competitiveness of Dutch firms across sectors.
Zowel de leden van de PvdA-fractie als de leden van de CDA-fractie vragen wat het vrijhandelsakkoord betekent voor de concurrentiepositie van Nederlandse bedrijven in verschillende sectoren.

v.summary: The Raad van State advisory division supports the EU-Korea free trade agreement bill but asks the government to clarify in the explanatory memorandum which parts fall within Dutch national competence, given the mixed nature of the agreement. The government's reply (nader rapport) states that a section on the nature of the agreement was added and that the article-by-article explanation now indicates where member states have their own competence; redactional remarks were followed.
concerns: The Afdeling asks for clarification of the mixed-agreement character and of which parts require Dutch parliamentary approval, which the government addressed by adding a paragraph and article-level notes.
Redactional remarks in the annex, including the interpretation of the 'reasonable period' criterion under GATT Article XXIV, were followed.

33036.s: The bill amends the Wet op de rechterlijke organisatie to create a second deputy chief public prosecutor at the Landelijk parket who serves as the Dutch national member of Eurojust, implementing part of the 2008 Eurojust decision amendment. It also provides that a senior public prosecutor acts as deputy to the national member, with the powers already available under the Code of Criminal Procedure.
33036.j: The memorandum justifies placing the national member as deputy chief prosecutor at the Landelijk parket so that the powers required by the Eurojust decision are exercisable within the existing structure of the public prosecution service.
q: By placing the national member functionally within the Landelijk parket, it is ensured that the member can exercise the nationally required powers, in line with the requirements of the amending decision.

Door het nationaal lid functioneel onder te brengen bij het landelijk parket is verzekerd dat deze de nationaal vereiste bevoegdheden kan uitoefenen, in overeenstemming met de eisen van het herzieningsbesluit.

parties: Asks whether Eurojust is effective, how its effectiveness is measured, its annual cost, and why the decision has not yet been implemented in Dutch law.
They ask what the state of Eurojust's effectiveness is.
Zij vragen hoe het staat met de effectiviteit van Eurojust?
Asks why the revision decision was not implemented on time and why one bill was not used, and questions the clarity of the national member's position and powers.
First they ask why it was not chosen to implement the revision decision in Dutch legislation in a single bill.
Allereerst vragen zij waarom niet gekozen is voor één wetsvoorstel, waarin het herzieningsbesluit in de Nederlandse wetgeving wordt geïmplementeerd.

Asks how authority is divided between the chief prosecutor and the deputy, whether the national member has powers a regular prosecutor lacks, and whether the national ministers are politically accountable.
In this context these members ask what the authority relationship is between the chief prosecutor at the national prosecutor's office and the (second) deputy chief prosecutor.
Deze leden vragen in dit kader hoe de gezagverhouding is tussen de hoofdofficier bij het landelijk parket en de (tweede) plaatsvervangend hoofdofficier bij het landelijk parket.
Views Eurojust as an important instrument against crime and supports strengthening it through the bill.
This bill contributes to strengthening Eurojust.
Dit wetsvoorstel draagt bij aan het versterken van Eurojust.

Asks whether Eurojust has sufficient powers and resources, why a European Public Prosecutor might be needed, and how the requirement that staff be prosecutors, judges or police officers is implemented.
According to the government, does Eurojust have sufficient possibilities and resources to carry out its tasks properly?
Heeft Eurojust volgens de regering voldoende mogelijkheden en middelen haar taken goed uit te voeren?

v.summary: The Afdeling advisering of the Raad van State supports the bill implementing Council Decision 2009/426/JBZ strengthening Eurojust, but asks that the explanatory memorandum be aligned with the bill's text by no longer describing the national member and deputy as appointed 'in tijdelijke dienst' under the rechtspositie rules, and gives redactional remarks. The minister's nader rapport accepts the point, amends the memorandum, and adopts the redactional remarks, with clarification of how implementation obligations will be met in practice.
concerns: The explanatory memorandum's references to appointment in temporary service should be brought in line with the bill's wording on designation for a fixed term.
Redactional remarks on the bill and memorandum are adopted, including clarifying how Dutch practice will meet implementation obligations and adding a cross-reference in the transposition table.

33045.s: The bill amends the Wet tegemoetkoming chronisch zieken en gehandicapten so that the allowance becomes conditional on income (draagkracht), with income ceilings, a partner definition aligned to the AWBZ, and income data obtained from the tax inspector. It also allows the CAK to recover allowances retroactively when income data change and sets the allowance amounts by general administrative order.
33045.j: The memorandum justifies the delegations as needed to apply the income test consistently with the Awir framework and to keep the allowance amounts and ceilings current each year.
q: Entitlement to an income-dependent allowance from the CAK belongs to persons in a group to be determined by or under a general administrative order in the calculation year.

Recht op een van de draagkracht afhankelijke tegemoetkoming van het CAK heeft degene die in het berekeningsjaar behoort tot een bij of krachtens algemene maatregel van bestuur te bepalen groep van personen
d: groups of persons entitled to the income-dependent allowance
amount of the allowance, which may differ per group
annual adjustment of income ceilings for allowance eligibility
data categories and cases for CAK data processing
technical standards, security requirements, data supply fees and deadlines
p: CAK may withdraw granted allowances and reclaim them retroactively when income data change, with fixed eight-week deadlines.](the bill sets deadlines but no hearing or proportionality requirement)
Article XVI of the 2009 tax measures, which bars certain retroactive corrections, is made inapplicable to CAK decisions under this law.
CAK gains broad access to health and income personal data, with the scope set by general administrative order and the security rules by ministerial regulation.

parties: Asks the minister to explain the administrative costs for the CAK and Belastingdienst and why different partner definitions are used, but does not raise a check concern.
Can the minister explain what the increased implementation costs are for both the CAK and the Belastingdienst?
Kan de minister toelichten wat de toegenomen uitvoeringslasten zijn voor zowel het CAK als voor de Belastingdienst?
Criticises the speed of the change without prior research or evaluation and asks for consultation of stakeholders and extensive study before the plenary debate.
Can the minister explain why she is already choosing to make the scheme income-dependent before the previously announced evaluation?
Kan de minister aangeven waarom zij voorafgaand aan de eerder aangekondigde evaluatie nu al kiest voor het inkomensafhankelijk maken van de regeling?
Questions the feasibility and fairness of the income reference year and partner definition, and asks for recalculation and possibilities to protect households with multiple illnesses.
In what way does the income from three years ago still say anything about the financial capacity of a household?
Op welke wijze zegt het inkomen van drie jaar geleden nog iets over de draagkracht van een huishouden?
Opposes the Wtcg system as opaque and bureaucratic, citing the Ombudsman, and asks the government to justify its choices, data-security safeguards and the income threshold basis.
On what basis does the government still cling to the bureaucratic Wtcg system, and why does it not choose to reintroduce the tax deduction for extraordinary care expenses?
Op grond waarvan houdt de regering dan vast aan de bureaucratische Wtcg-systematiek, en kiest zij niet voor herinvoering van de belastingaftrek buitengewone zorguitgaven?
Accepts the income-dependence in principle but asks about privacy safeguards for data exchange, transition arrangements for affected groups, and notification of those denied benefits.
Is the government willing to examine a transitional arrangement for this group of chronically ill and disabled people?
Is de regering bereid voor deze groep chronisch zieken en gehandicapten een overgangsregeling te onderzoeken?
Questions the basis for the income thresholds and whether the scheme still adequately compensates chronically ill people, and challenges the motion cited in the explanatory memorandum.
Why is this motion nevertheless cited in the explanatory memorandum?
Waarom wordt deze motie in de Memorie van Toelichting toch aangehaald?

33063.s: The bill amends the Dutch Wet veiligheid en kwaliteit lichaamsmateriaal and the Wet op de orgaandonatie to implement EU Directive 2010/53/EU on quality and safety standards for human organs intended for transplantation. It adds definitions, quality and safety chapter requirements, a register of procurement organisations and transplant centres, traceability and data-protection rules, and rules on organ exchange with non-EU countries.
33063.j: The memorandum justifies the changes as necessary to implement Directive 2010/53/EU and states that the procedures and quality requirements are elaborated in the directive's articles, with no explicit justification of new executive discretion.
q: The protocol on quality and safety is consistent with the rules the EU organ transplantation directive lays down for this protocol.
Het protocol inzake kwaliteit en veiligheid is in overeenstemming met de regels die de EU-richtlijn orgaantransplantatie met betrekking tot dit protocol stelt.
d: designation of the EU tissue/cell and organ transplantation directives
orgaancentrum protocol on quality and safety across the donation chain
minister to compile updated register of procurement organisations and transplant centres
technical requirements under the EU tissue and cell directive for tissue institutions, preparation techniques and donor laboratory tests
orgaancentrum agreements with counterparts in third countries for organ exchange

parties: Asks whether implementation will add rules, barriers and administrative burden, and whether the non-profit requirement conflicts with planned regulated profit distribution in healthcare.
These members ask to what extent the implementation of the directive, based on these flexible formulations, is expected to lead to additional rules and barriers and increased administrative burden.

Deze leden vragen in hoeverre de implementatie van de richtlijn, gebaseerd op deze flexibele formuleringen, naar verwachting zal leiden tot extra regels en barrières en toegenomen administratieve lasten.
Asks which adjustments Dutch hospitals must make, what improvements the system gains, what the administrative burden is, and whether doctors' associations were consulted.
These members attach great importance to a safe and efficient system for obtaining donor organs.
Deze leden hechten groot belang aan een veilig en efficiënt systeem voor het verkrijgen van donororganen.

33090-IIA.s: This bill amends the 2011 budget of the Dutch Staten-Generaal (parliament) to reflect supplementary budget changes made in the spring and autumn 2011 updates. It sets the budget in thousands of euros and provides for entry into force from 1 December 2011.
q: The budget statement of the Staten-Generaal for the year 2011 is amended, as shown in the statement attached to this law.
De begrotingsstaat van de Staten-Generaal voor het jaar 2011 wordt gewijzigd, zoals blijkt uit de desbetreffende bij deze wet behorende staat.

33108.s: The bill makes technical corrections to the Dutch civil court fee act (Wet griffierechten burgerlijke zaken) and the Code of Civil Procedure, including fee rules for appeals, joinder, default judgments and a new court power to cap the fee a losing party must pay. It does not delegate rule-making power to the executive and does not expand executive discretion.
33108.j: The memorandum justifies the new hardship clause by pointing to concerns raised in the Eerste Kamer and advice from the Raad van State that natural persons should not bear high corporate fee rates in small collection cases.
q: According to this new fifth paragraph, the court may determine that the court fee of the prevailing party, which must be paid by the losing party as part of the cost award, is not higher than the court fee paid by that losing party.

Volgens dit nieuwe vijfde lid kan de rechter bepalen dat het griffierecht van de in het gelijk gestelde partij, dat in het kader van de proceskostenveroordeling betaald moet worden door de in het ongelijk gestelde partij, niet hoger is dan het griffierecht dat van deze laatste partij is geheven.
p: Artikel II, onderdeel E (artikel 237 Rv, vijfde lid)
Gives courts discretion to cap the fee a losing party must pay, protecting citizens against high cost awards where the outcome would be unfair.

parties: Questions whether abolishing the distinction between natural and legal persons should be reconsidered, since businesses can deduct fees from profits while individuals usually cannot, and asks about the hardship clause.
Court fees can after all be deducted from profits by businesses, and that is usually not the case for private individuals.
Griffierechten kunnen immers door bedrijven van hun winst worden afgetrokken en dat is voor particulieren meestal niet het geval.
Argues the government has not kept its promise to the Senate to lower fees for legal persons in small debt cases, and that equalising fees raises absolute costs for natural persons.

In the view of these members, equalising court fees for natural and legal persons removes the inequality between them, but also means natural persons will have to pay more court fees in absolute terms.

Naar de mening van de aan het woord zijnde leden betekent het gelijktrekken van de griffierechten van natuurlijke en rechtspersonen weliswaar dat de ongelijkheid tussen beide wordt opgeheven, maar heeft dat ook tot gevolg dat natuurlijke personen in absolute zin meer griffierechten moeten gaan betalen.
Asks the government to respond to the Dutch judges' association's point about unclear rules on whether a judge may disregard a late defence submission when the fee is unpaid.
When a defence submission is filed in the same case, whether the judge may disregard that submission depends on whether the required court fee was paid on time.

Wanneer in dezelfde zaak een verweerschrift wordt ingediend, is het antwoord op de vraag of de rechter op dat verweerschrift acht mag slaan afhankelijk van de vraag of het verschuldigde griffierecht op tijd is betaald.

Worries that small non-incorporated businesses and sole traders will face steep fee increases that impair their ability to enforce or defend rights, and asks how default judgments will be communicated.
How will the government prevent these parties from being unable to enforce or defend their rights?
Hoe gaat de regering voorkomen dat deze partijen hun recht niet meer kunnen halen of verdedigen?

Argues the government has not met its Senate commitment, since the hardship clause gives limited protection and the pending fee increase would substantially raise debts for people already in financial trouble.
The aforementioned members note that the government has therefore not honoured its commitment to the Senate.
Voornoemde leden constateren dat de regering daarom niet is tegemoetgekomen aan haar toezegging aan de Eerste Kamer.

v.summary: The Afdeling advisering of the Raad van State supports the Reparatiewet griffierechten burgerlijke zaken but advises revising the removal of the obligation to state the court fee in the summons and adding a hardship clause for natural persons ordered to pay the higher corporate fee, plus a coordination provision with the parallel fee-increase bill. The minister's reply adopts the advice on the summons, the hardship clause and the drafting note, but declines a coordination provision because the amendments are substantively identical and the repair act is expected to enter into force first.
concerns: Removing the obligation to state the court fee in the summons would place the risk of paying a wrong amount on the defendant, so the summons should instead refer to the latest fee table, which the minister adopted.

Natural persons and insolvent defendants facing the higher corporate fee in cantonal cases in cost orders need a hardship clause, which the minister adopted via a new fifth paragraph of article 237 Rv.
A coordination provision is needed between this bill and the parallel fee-increase bill, which the minister declined as unnecessary because the repair act is expected to take effect first.
The editorial note on the removal of the term gemachtigde in article 111 Rv and article 276 Rv was adopted with an added explanation in the commentary.

33126.s: The bill amends the Civil Code, the Code of Civil Procedure and the Bankruptcy Act to improve collective settlement of mass claims under the WCAM, including tighter admissibility for claim foundations, joinder and referral powers, a court-directed regulation hearing, changes to notice and publication, and rules on bankruptcy trustees concluding such settlements. It also removes the verification phase for claims covered by a declared-binding trustee settlement.
33126.j: The memorandum justifies the changes by evaluation findings that the WCAM is efficient and effective, and by the need to curb abusive claim foundations and conflicting parallel actions.
q: A legal person referred to in paragraph 1 is likewise inadmissible if the interests of the persons on whose behalf the claim is brought are insufficiently safeguarded by the action.

Een rechtspersoon als bedoeld in lid 1 is eveneens niet ontvankelijk, indien met de rechtsvordering de belangen van de personen ten behoeve van wie de rechtsvordering is ingesteld onvoldoende gewaarborgd zijn.
p: Adds admissibility requirements for claim organisations and empowers courts to refer or join mass claims ex officio, tightening access to collective action.
Removes cassation appeal against approval of settlements and limits the grounds for royement, narrowing affected parties' procedural remedies, while adding notice and publication duties.

Removes the verification phase for creditors with claims under a binding trustee settlement and bars the bankrupt from contesting such settlements, limiting individual creditors' ability to dispute claims, subject to rechter-commissaris approval and court review.

parties: Asks about balancing efficient mass claim settlement against the risk of a claims paradise, and about the opt-out and court control of implementation.
In view of these concerns, they ask the government to clearly explain how it views the balance between efficient claiming on the one hand and the risk of a claims paradise on the other.

Zij vragen de regering met het oog op deze zorgen, nog eens helder uiteen te zetten hoe zij aankijkt tegen de balans tussen efficiënt claimen aan de ene kant en het risico van een claimparadijs aan de andere kant.
Supports the preprocedural comparison and the judge's advisory role, while asking whether the representativeness requirement's removal increases or decreases admissible claim organisations.
However, they are of the view that it is important that a dispute is brought to a good conclusion, preferably by the parties themselves.
Zij zijn echter van mening dat het belangrijk is dat een geschil tot een goed eind wordt gebracht, bij voorkeur door de partijen zelf.
Asks whether the removal of the representativeness requirement provides sufficient tools to curb the proliferation of claim foundations.

Can the government indicate whether the criterion that the interests of the represented persons must be sufficiently safeguarded will provide sufficient tools to counter the proliferation and problems of claim foundations?

Kan de regering aangegeven of het criterium dat de belangen van de vertegenwoordigde personen voldoende gewaarborgd dienen te zijn, voldoende handvatten zal bieden om de wildgroei en de problemen bij claimstichtingen tegen te gaan?

Questions whether the representativeness requirement is firm enough, the legal status of the claim code, transparency of claim foundations, and risks of the opt-out system and foreign claims in the Netherlands.
These members are of the view that the door should not be opened too wide for foreign parties to settle their international claim cases in the Netherlands from now on.
Deze leden zijn van oordeel dat de deur voor buitenlandse partijen om hun internationale claimzaken voortaan in Nederland af te wikkelen, niet te wijd moet worden opengezet.
Supports the WCAM but questions the very open new admissibility norm, asking how judges can test whether interests are safeguarded and what remedies rejected foundations have.

It is good that the judge receives a handle to critically assess the admissibility of a collective action, however the new norm proposed in article 3:105a, second paragraph, Civil Code is drafted very openly.

Het is goed dat de rechter een handvat krijgt om kritisch te oordelen over de ontvankelijkheid van een collectieve actie, de nieuwe norm die wordt voorgesteld in artikel 3:105a, tweede lid, BW is echter zeer open opgesteld.

v.summary: The Raad van State advisory division supports the bill extending the WCAM collective settlement regime, but objects to the open representativeness requirement, the proposed preprocessual comparitie (judge's new role), and the use of WCAM in bankruptcy, advising to drop the first and second and to study alternatives and clarify the bankruptcy regime. The government reply adopts the representativeness deletion and the bankruptcy clarifications but rejects dropping the preprocessual comparitie, arguing the judge's facilitative role already exists in other procedures.
concerns: The open representativeness norm in art. 3:305a BW is vague and would lead to divergent assessments and legal uncertainty, so the requirement is to be dropped.
The preprocessual comparitie substantially changes the civil judge's role from dispute-settler to mediator before any proceedings exist; the Afdeling advises against it.
Alternatives to applying WCAM in bankruptcy (e.g. surseance rules, rechter-commissaris review) should be studied and the bill adjusted where needed; the government explains why WCAM was preferred.
Position of other creditors (paritas creditorum), the contestation route, and the precise content and binding effect of a WCAM settlement in bankruptcy are unclear and must be explained and amended.
The wording of the new art. 7:907 lid 7 BW is too indefinite and should be clarified, which was done.

33135.s: The bill makes the Crisis- and herstelwet permanent by removing its 1 January 2014 expiry, and amends several environmental and spatial planning laws (Wabo, Wro, Wm, Wet luchtvaart, Nbwet, Wet geluidhinder and others) to streamline permits, update reference dates and replace references to the Milieu- en Natuurplanbureau with the Planbureau voor de Leefomgeving. It also shortens the procedure for temporary planning deviations, allows two-year-old data to be used, and changes the planning-damage and noise-exemption rules.
33135.j: The memorandum justifies the flexibility and speed gains by pointing to positive evaluation results of the Chw and the need to respond quickly to societal wishes such as temporary reuse of vacant offices.
q: The government proposes to abolish the separate procedural variant for this type of environmental permit.
De regering stelt voor om de afzonderlijke procedurevariant voor dit type omgevingsvergunningen af te schaffen.
d: categories of activities with time-limited permits and seasonal structures
competent authority imposing new techniques on existing permits
rules for discharges outside installations under general rules
p: Permit authorities gain wider discretion to grant temporary deviations and time-limited permits without the extended procedure, with the reasoning requirement as main safeguard.
Permitting authorities may rely on data up to two years old, subject to judicial review of the reasoning.
Noise-related deviations for permits are exempted from the normal procedure.

parties: Supports permanence for faster projects but asks how the act relates to the Omgevingswet and whether earlier environmental concerns were justified.
The VVD members support making the Crisis- and herstelwet permanent because it accelerates the implementation of spatial projects in a careful manner.
De leden van de VVD-fractie zijn voorstander van het permanent maken van de Crisis- en herstelwet omdat deze de uitvoering van ruimtelijke projecten op een zorgvuldige manier versnelt.
Worries that the act reduces citizens' say over their surroundings and legal protection, and that fast procedures are not the real fix for the housing market.
Citizens' control over their own environment is becoming less and less.
De zeggenschap van burgers over hun eigen omgeving wordt minder en minder.
Supports permanence and argues the evaluations show the act works, while asking the government to confirm the reasoning for a solid permanent framework.
There is more than sufficient basis to assume that the Crisis- and herstelwet works well.
Er is meer dan voldoende basis om aan te nemen dat de Crisis- en herstelwet goed werkt.
Objects that the evaluation is not awaited, the Raad van State is critical, and the legal uncertainty of an indefinite temporary law is problematic.
In the view of the SP members, the present proposal has almost become a political semantic debate.
Naar de mening van de leden van de SP-fractie is bij onderhavig voorstel inmiddels bijna sprake van een politiek semantische discussie.
Has great concerns that the act limits public participation and careful process, and that the government did not adequately answer the Raad van State's objections.
These members question whether the Crisis- and herstelwet truly contributes to recovery or instead limits public participation and hinders a careful process.
Deze leden vragen zich af of de Crisis- en herstelwet een werkelijke bijdrage levert aan herstel en niet juist zorgt voor het beperken van inspraak en het tegengaan van een zorgvuldig proces.
Sees the act as sidelining civil society and municipalities, questions environmental protection and the reduction of inspection and legal protection.
Will public participation and legal protection of citizens decrease?
Wordt de inspraak en rechtsbescherming van burgers minder?
Questions the indefinite extension without evaluation, asks for a problem analysis, and worries about permanent environmental impact assessment exemptions.
They therefore endorse the Raad van State's view that a problem analysis is indeed necessary when provisions are made (semi-)permanent.
Zij onderschrijven dan ook de mening van de Raad van State dat er wel degelijk een probleemanalyse noodzakelijk is wanneer bepalingen (semi)permanent worden gemaakt.
Opposes permanence without evaluation, arguing the act undermines nature, environmental and citizens' legal protection and has been partly corrected by Raad van State rulings.
Setting aside carefully enacted legislation that must protect citizens, the environment and nature can, as far as the Party for the Animals members are concerned, never be justified.

Het buiten werking stellen van wetgeving die zorgvuldig tot stand gekomen is, die burgers, het milieu en de natuur moet beschermen, kan wat de leden van de fractie van de Partij voor de Dieren betreft nooit gerechtvaardigd worden.
Supports the goals of cutting burdens and speeding decisions but notes the lack of evaluation and doubts about whether the act has substantive effect.
Nevertheless, these members consider it a disadvantage that the agreed evaluation of the Crisis- and herstelwet is not being awaited.
Desalniettemin achten deze leden het een nadeel dat niet de afgesproken evaluatie van de Crisis- en herstelwet wordt afgewacht.
Worries that limits on objection and appeal grounds, lex silencio positivo and the six-month court deadline weaken citizens' legal protection and access to the judge.
The PvdA members are concerned about the position of the citizen.
De leden van de PvdA-fractie maken zich zorgen over de positie van de burger.
Strongly favours making the Chw's provisions permanent and anchoring them in law, citing the evaluation and business support.
The CDA members again state that they attach great value to making permanent and anchoring the provisions in the Chw.
De leden van de CDA-fractie willen opnieuw uitspreken dat zij veel waarde hechten aan het permanent maken en verankeren van de voorzieningen die in de Chw zijn opgenomen.
Questions the broad scope of the Chw, the lack of project-level evaluation and the displacement effects, and asks whether the bill should be withdrawn.
Considering all objections, the SP members ask whether the bill in this form should not be withdrawn.
Alle bezwaren overziende vragen de leden van de SP-fractie of het wetsvoorstel in deze vorm niet ingetrokken moet worden.
Not convinced of the need to make the Chw permanent before evaluation and the Omgevingswet; asks for a problem analysis and citizen perspective.
These members thank the government for the extensive reply but are by no means convinced of the necessity and usefulness of making the Chw permanent.
Deze leden danken de regering voor de uitgebreide beantwoording, maar zijn nog geenszins overtuigd van nut en noodzaak om de Chw permanent te maken en hebben nog een aantal vragen en opmerkingen.
Doubts the permanence of the procedural restrictions, the MER relaxation and the relativity requirement, citing threats to access to the judge and displacement of other cases.
This evaluation strengthens these members in the conviction that it is too early to make the Chw permanent.
Deze evaluatie sterkt deze leden in de overtuiging dat het te vroeg is om de Chw perma nent te maken.
Argues the Chw sets aside environmental and citizen protections, restricts access to justice contrary to the Aarhus Convention, and calls for broader evaluation before permanence.
This law, which sets aside dozens of laws protecting nature, the environment and citizens' rights, is inherently controversial.
Deze wet, die tientallen wetten ter bescher ming van de natuur, het milieu en rechten van burgers opzij zet, is bij uitstek controversieel.

v.summary: The Raad van State's Afdeling advisering supports the nota van wijziging to the Crisis- en herstelwet but objects that no compensation rule was included for the new article 2.3 powers and that the Natuurbeschermingswet exemption is unclearly formulated and wider than the explanatory memorandum intends. The minister's nader rapport accepts the compensation point, adds an explicit reference to article 4.2 Wabo, and revises the Nbw exemption wording and explanatory memorandum to meet most remarks.
concerns: The exemption from the Natura 2000 permit requirement was formulated more broadly than the explanatory memorandum intended, and the Afdeling asked for alignment with the memorandum and clearer wording.
The explanatory memorandum's conditions for the exemption, such as the project staying within assessed effects, were absent from the statutory text and needed to be added.

Absence of a compensation rule for damage from changed permit conditions under the new article 2.3 Chw created inequality with the Wabo, which the Afdeling asked to remedy by applying article 4.2 Wabo.
The Afdeling asked the explanatory memorandum to address the actuality of the appropriate assessment, the flexibility of zoning, and the administrative burdens on initiators.
The Afdeling asked that the consultation advice of IPO, VNG and Unie van Waterschappen be sent along with the nota; the government explained it had obtained only staff-level input due to urgency.
Several redactional remarks on the wording of the Chw and Nbw 1998 provisions were noted, with most adopted and splitting of article 2.3 Chw declined.

v.summary: The Afdeling advisering of the Raad van State advised on a bill to make the temporary Crisis- en herstelwet permanent and to introduce several environmental-law 'quick wins', raising serious objections on procedural basis, delegation, legal certainty, and the decentralised governments' right of appeal. The minister's nader rapport accepted the Afdeling's alternative of extending the Chw's duration and deferring permanent anchoring to separate Awb and Omgevingswet bills, so most of the bill's substance was withdrawn.
concerns: The Afdeling found no problem analysis or evidence (evaluation results) justifying permanent anchoring of the temporary Chw; the government followed the alternative of extending the Chw and awaiting the evaluation.
The Afdeling objected to the uniform Awb procedure being fragmented and to the post-annulment fact-finding rule, which the government largely deferred or addressed by withdrawing the provisions.

Essential procedural rules (access to court, handling of disputes) were proposed to be delegated to an amvb, contrary to the primacy of the legislature; the government moved these matters to separate bills.

Concerns about legal protection of individuals, legal certainty and equal treatment, and the restriction of decentralised governments' right to appeal, were raised; the government largely withdrew or deferred these elements.

The Afdeling warned that the 'omgevingsvergunning-plus', innovation experiments without a term, and single-instance appeal create uncertainty and complexity; several of these were removed or deferred.

33162.s: The bill restricts export of Dutch child benefit to children not living in the Netherlands, removing the treaty-based exception, and adds transitional rules for people living in treaty countries when a treaty is terminated or amended. It makes parallel transitional provisions in the General Old Age Act, General Surviving Relatives Act, disability insurance laws, Sickness Benefits Act and Toeslagenwet, and delegates to the government the power to announce which countries are affected and when.
33162.j: The memorandum justifies the export restriction by the limited control powers of Dutch agencies abroad, aiming to improve compliance with the territoriality principle, and cites costs and the need for proportionality.
q: To stop the export of child benefit to treaty countries, the current exception for treaty situations is removed.
Om de export van kinderbijslag naar verdragslanden stop te zetten, wordt de huidige uitzondering die geldt voor verdragssituaties geschrapt.
d: exceptions to child benefit export restriction for workers in general interest, Aruba/Curaçao/Sint Maarten and Bonaire/Sint Eustatius/Saba residents, and family members
minister announces countries and dates when treaties cease or are amended
royal decree sets entry into force and retroactive dates, possibly differing per article
p: Removes the treaty-based entitlement to child benefit for children living abroad, narrowing protections for citizens and extending executive control over benefit eligibility.
Limits transitional protection to two quarters after treaty termination, with the minister determining the affected countries and dates."},{

parties: Asks for the number of persons affected, treaty renegotiation timelines, and the criteria for terminating treaties, and questions whether the transitional rules infringe property rights.
They support the government's intention to restrict the export of benefits to countries outside the EU.
Zij steunen de regering in het voornemen om de export van uitkeringen naar landen buiten de EU te beperken.
Asks which treaty partners may refuse cooperation, how affected citizens will be informed, and the arguments against terminating treaties.
How are citizens who will face the consequences of this bill informed by the government?
Hoe worden burgers die te maken krijgen met de consequenties van dit wetsvoorstel geïnformeerd door de regering?

Asks for estimates of the numbers affected, the consequences of treaty termination, and whether the minister's earlier commitment to prioritise the countries receiving most benefits is being implemented; also questions retroactive application.
In which situations will the bill be introduced with retroactive effect, and what could be a reason for this?
In welke situaties wordt het wetsvoorstel met terugwerkende kracht ingevoerd en wat kan hiervoor een reden zijn?

Asks how feasible termination of the 21 bilateral treaties is, how this relates to EU efforts and the ECHR and treaty fidelity, and why retroactive regulation and differing transitional rules were chosen.
How does terminating the contracts relate to the European Convention on Human Rights (ECHR) and international treaty fidelity?
Hoe verhoudt het opzeggen van de contracten zich tot het Europees Verdrag ter bescherming van de rechten van de mens en de fundamentele vrijheden (EVRM) en de internationale verdragstrouw?

Questions the legal consistency of denying a general benefit to parents who still pay taxes, and asks about consequences for children studying or living abroad for medical or custody reasons, requesting exceptions.
Can the government explain whether it is legally correct that parents no longer have a right to a general provision while they still contribute to it through taxes?
Kan de regering toelichten of het juridisch juist is dat ouders geen recht meer hebben op een algemene voorziening terwijl zij via de belastingen wel mee betalen aan deze algemene voorziening?

Asks about international practice, whether other countries will agree to amendments only in exchange for concessions, and warns that the export goal must not produce treaty changes less favourable to the Netherlands.

Does the government share the view that stopping exports must not be a matter of principle in the sense that this ambition must not lead to treaty changes that on balance turn out less favourably for the Netherlands?

Deelt de regering de mening van de leden dat het stopzetten van de export geen principieel punt mag zijn in de zin dat deze ambitie niet mag leiden tot verdragswijzigingen die per saldo minder gunstig uitpakken voor Nederland?

Asks how the situation is judged for legal equality if some countries do not cooperate, how legal certainty is affected by retroactivity, and why a discretionary provision was chosen for the Caribbean territories.
Does this not come at the expense of legal certainty for those involved?
Gaat dit niet ten koste van de rechtszekerheid van de betrokkenen?

v.summary: The Council of State's advisory division supports the bill ending child benefit and child-linked budget exports to non-EU countries but raises objections on international law, EU Charter Article 17 (property), Union loyalty, transitional law and Turkey, and advises adaptation. The government's reply accepts most points by supplementing the explanatory memorandum, though it rejects the Turkey and transitional-law objections in part.
concerns: The Council asks for justification of the bill's consistency with EU associations-level developments and contact with the European Commission, and the government added this reasoning to the memorandum.
The Council asks the bill to be tested against Article 17(1) of the EU Charter on property, and the government added a passage applying the ECHR Protocol 1 standard.

The Council notes affected persons may not understand why entitlement ends where the treaties are unchanged and legitimate expectations may be breached, and the government supplemented the memorandum regarding the countries concerned.

The Council says the transitional rule may conflict with treaty clauses preserving acquired rights and asks the memorandum to address SVB's comment, which the government addressed with a quarterly-system explanation.
The Council says the Turkey treaty may contain an export obligation and asks for supplementation, and the government clarified that Article 33 contains only an equal-treatment obligation.

The Council asks for analysis of the treaties lacking an explicit export-limitation clause and of non-cooperation by treaty partners, including diplomatic side effects, which the government addressed only partially.

33171.s: The bill implements EU Directive 2011/7 on late payment in commercial transactions by amending Book 6 of the Dutch Civil Code: it sets a default 30-day payment term, a maximum 60-day term by agreement, a mandatory minimum recovery-cost fee of 40 euro, and a statutory commercial interest rate that applies to government bodies. It also adds a transitional provision so that the new rules do not apply to contracts concluded before entry into force.
33171.j: The memorandum justifies the delegation to an general administrative order by stating that the recovery-cost system is further specified by regulation so that it aligns with the directive's collection-cost rules.
d: ARTIKEL I, A (artikel 96 lid 6 BW, nieuw)
recovery cost compensation system for out-of-court collection costs

parties: Asks what counts as additional collection costs, whether the 40 euro minimum harms firms, and how contractual freedom and the justification criteria for longer payment terms will be made concrete.
These members attach great importance to the freedom of contract that underlies Dutch civil law.
Deze leden hechten groot belang aan de contractsvrijheid die ten grondslag ligt aan het Nederlands burgerlijk recht.
Asks why no maximum collection-cost compensation was set alongside the minimum, the relation to the existing decree on extrajudicial collection costs, and the financial consequences for the state.
The aforementioned members ask why, alongside a minimum compensation for collection costs, a maximum compensation was not also introduced.
De leden van de PVV-fractie vragen waarom er naast een minimumvergoeding voor invorderingskosten ook niet over is gegaan tot een maximumvergoeding voor invorderingskosten.
Questions why the Council of State's advice to set the 40 euro amount by general administrative order was not followed, given the need for flexibility and legal certainty.

Viewed against this background, the aforementioned members ask why the advice of the Council of State's advisory division was not followed and why implementation via a general administrative order would not suffice.
Tegen deze achtergrond bezien, vragen voornoemde leden waarom het advies van de Afdeling advisering niet is gevolgd en waarom implementatie via een algemene maatregel van bestuur niet volstaat.

Worries that exceptions in the government payment rules will be used too often, that large firms can force small suppliers into longer terms, and that small firms cannot practically litigate, so the bill offers no real protection.
This bill offers no solution for that, because it is still possible to deviate from the statutory 60-day term.
Daar biedt dit wetsvoorstel geen oplossing voor, omdat nog steeds kan worden afgeweken van de wettelijke termijn van 60 dagen.

Asks whether decentralised governments can realistically meet the 30-day deadline, what causes late payment, and how effects will be monitored and evaluated, and how abuse of agreed longer terms is prevented.
They ask how it is prevented that a large company forces a smaller supplier to extend the terms.
Zij vragen hoe wordt voorkomen dat een groot bedrijf een kleinere leverancier dwingt tot verruiming van de voorwaarden.

v.summary: The Afdeling advisering of the Raad van State advised on a bill implementing Directive 2011/7/EU on late payments in commercial transactions into Boek 6 BW, supporting its aim but raising implementation concerns about strict and precise transposition, express agreement on longer payment terms, and drafting points. The government's nader rapport accepted most points, including adjusting the wording on express contractual agreement and objective justification, and noted a translation error in the Dutch version of the Directive.
concerns: Article 6:119b(4) BW must expressly reflect that a longer acceptance term must be stated in both the contract and any tender documents, as required by Article 4(5) of the Directive.
The phrase 'objective justification' in Article 6:119b(5) should be left to legal practice rather than being filled in by the unfair-terms criteria of Article 7(1) of the Directive.
The criterion of a considerable departure from good commercial practice should be transposed more precisely, in line with the Directive's text.
Article 6:119a(5) should make clear that a longer payment term between businesses must be expressly included in the contract, not merely agreed in general terms.

Several redactional comments on numbering, cross-references, terminology and placement of transitional provisions are given, with the 40 euro collection-cost amount retained in the statute for clarity.

33207.s: The bill tightens sanctions for benefit fraud and non-compliance across Dutch social security laws (Toeslagenwet, WW, WAO, WIA, Ziektewet, WWB, Kinderbijslag and others) by introducing or raising administrative fines, extending the recidivism window to five or ten years, and allowing recovery of fines by fully offsetting future benefits, including suspension of the subsistence allowance (beslagvrije voet). It also lets the executive set fine levels by general administrative order and waive fines or recovery by ministerial regulation-based criteria.
33207.j: The memorandum justifies the stronger sanctions as necessary to protect solidarity and public funds against fraud, and says the general administrative orders will set criteria for severe measures.
q: Fraud must not pay
Fraude mag niet lonen
d: manner of enforcing administrative fine decisions
Artikel 91 lid 10 (WAO/WIA-equivalent, WWB/ Wet werk en inkomen naar arbeidsvermogen)
nadere regels on height of administrative fine
p: Administrative fines up to 150 percent of the benefit overpayment are imposed on recidivists, with a ten-year window where prior imprisonment occurred, widening executive sanction power over benefit recipients.
Fines may be recovered by full offset against ongoing benefits for up to five years, with the subsistence allowance disapplied, limiting the protection of recipients against state recovery.
The appeal court may increase the fine against the claimant, departing from the usual prohibition on reformatio in peius.

parties: Asks how municipalities' discretion and the hardship clause will be applied and how non-compliance by municipalities will be prevented.
These members ask when there are undesirable consequences and when there are not.
Deze leden vragen wanneer er sprake is van onwenselijke gevolgen en wanneer niet?
Argues the bill breaches human rights and removes proportionality and access to the courts through mandatory sanctions and higher court fees.
The bill assumes every wrongly obtained benefit was deliberate fraud, automatically imposes a sanction, and at the same time blocks access to the court for the citizen through higher court fees.

Het wetsvoorstel gaat er vanuit dat elke onterecht verkregen uitkering bewuste fraude is geweest, legt automatisch een sanctie op, en verhindert voor de rechtzoekende tegelijkertijd de toegang tot de rechter door hogere griffierechten om recht te halen.
Supports strict enforcement against fraud and asks mainly factual questions about municipal implementation.
These members want, precisely to protect social security, strict enforcement and a hard-line approach to abuse, fraud and deceit.
Deze leden willen juist ter bescherming van de sociale zekerheid een strenge handhaving en keiharde aanpak van misbruik, fraude en bedrog.

Supports sanctions in principle but objects that the bill obliges municipalities to recover and enforce, removing their discretion, and questions the broad definition of fraud and the suspension of the protected minimum.
Why does the government want to restrict the policy discretion municipalities have had until now?
Waarom wil de regering de beleidsvrijheid die gemeenten tot nu toe hebben beperken?
Questions the constitutionality and ECHR compatibility of suspending the protected minimum and the far-reaching collection powers of the bestuurlijke boete.
Can the government explain how this measure relates to the constitution, which provides that every Dutch national has a right to the applicable subsistence minimum?
Kan de regering toelichten hoe deze maatregel zich verhoudt tot de grondwet waarin is opgenomen dat elke Nederlander recht heeft op het geldende bestaansminimum?
Asks why suspending the protected minimum is proportionate and compatible with ECHR Article 6 and Article 11 WWB, and whether the Raad voor de Rechtspraak was consulted.
These members want to know how suspending the protected minimum under the WWB relates to Article 11 of the Work and Assistance Act.
Deze leden willen weten hoe het buiten werking stellen van de beslagvrije voet in de WWB zich verhoudt met artikel 11 van de Wet werk en bijstand.

v.summary: The Raad van State advisory division advised on the draft Wet aanscherping handhaving en sanctiebeleid SZW-wetgeving, raising serious objections to necessity, the criminal-charge character and proportionality of recidive exclusion from benefits, the preventive last onder dwangsom, the shift from criminal to administrative sanctioning, and the duty of care regarding assistance, and advised reconsideration. The minister's reply largely accepts the points: the benefit exclusion and preventive dwangsom are dropped, recidive fines are raised to 150%, and the remaining arguments on sanctions and terminology are defended.
concerns: The Afdeling found the argument for a sharp sanction increase insufficiently substantiated and asked for proof that existing enforcement tools are inadequate; the government defended the measure with additional data and evaluation evidence.
The cumulation of multi-year benefit exclusion with high fines was judged disproportionate, and the government dropped the recidive benefit exclusion.

Benefit exclusion was judged a criminal charge under Article 6 ECHR and a violation of Article 1 First Protocol, lacking appealable decisions and ne bis in idem safeguards; the government dropped the measure.
The preventive last onder dwangsom departs from Article 5:7 Awb and takes on a punitive character; the government decided not to proceed with it.

The duty of care for assistance under the Constitution and European social charters was not respected in the three-month total exclusion from bijstand; the government limited the measure to discretionary cases with leenbijstand options.

The Afdeling noted that shifting from criminal to administrative enforcement needs justification under the criteria of the cabinet's sanction-choice memorandum; the government defended the shift with the closed-context argument.
The Afdeling asked that court fees not be charged in appeals against administrative sanctions; the government kept the existing practice.

The Afdeling asked that the term fraud be used only for deceit and that the explanatory memorandum match the text on the stillegging measure; the government kept the broad term but clarified the memorandum.

33240-V.s: This bill formally amends the 2011 departmental budget statement of the Ministry of Foreign Affairs and the budget statement of the CBI trading-services agency, as set out in the attached supplementary budget tables. It also fixes the amounts in thousands of euros and sets the entry-into-force date as the day after Staatsblad publication, retroactive to 31 December of the budget year.
q: Article 4 This act enters into force on the day after the date of issue of the Staatsblad in which it is published and has retroactive effect to 31 December of the budget year in question.

Artikel 4 Deze wet treedt in werking met ingang van de dag na de datum van uitgifte van het Staatsblad waarin zij wordt geplaatst en werkt terug tot en met 31 december van het onderhavige begrotingsjaar.

33243.s: The bill transfers existing quality-of-care and workforce-structure tasks to a single independent body, the Nederlands Zorginstituut (NZi), which will maintain a public register of professional standards and quality indicators, collect quality data, and advise on quality matters via a new Adviescommissie Kwaliteit. It also amends the Zorgverzekeringswet and related laws to rename the College voor zorgverzekeringen and enables the Zorgautoriteit to issue instructions, orders, fines and penalties against providers who fail to report quality information.
33243.j: The memorandum justifies the delegated rule-making and new powers by the absence of a clear quality framework, the fragmentation of responsibilities, and the public interest in reliable quality information for consumers and supervisors.
q: The care system will work better when everyone knows what the norm for good care is and everyone can know whether care is delivered in line with that norm.
Het zorgstelsel zal beter werken wanneer iedereen weet wat de norm is voor goede zorg én iedereen kan weten of de zorg ook in overeenstemming met deze norm wordt geleverd.
d: Artikel I, E (Art. 47a, 2) / Artikel II, P (Art. 66b, 2)
beleidsregel on whether a professional standard qualifies for the public register
Artikel I, E (Art. 47c, 3) / Artikel II, P (Art. 66d, 3)
designating the body to which providers submit quality information
further rules on which data are included in the mandatory documents and when and to whom they are submitted
Artikel I, E (Art. 47d, 7) / Artikel II, P (Art. 59b reference)
reimbursement of travel and other costs for Adviescommissie Kwaliteit members
p: Artikel I, E (Art. 47c) / Artikel II, P (Art. 66d) / Artikel IV-X (Wmg enforcement)

The Zorginstituut and the Zorgautoriteit gain powers to collect quality information from providers and enforce its reporting through instructions, penalty payments and administrative fines, subject to general administrative law review.
Artikel IV, D-G and I (Wmg Art. 78a, 81a, 84a, 90)

The Zorgautoriteit may issue binding instructions, orders under administrative coercion, penalty payments and fines directly to providers for failing to report quality data, with the instruction power excluded for individual cases.

parties: Asks about budget, capacity, the risk that professional standards stifle innovation, sanctioning powers of NZi, NZa and IGZ, and whether the Adviescommissie Kwaliteit has enough information.
The Kwaliteitsinstituut will describe norms for good care in professional standards.
Het Kwaliteitsinstituut gaat normen voor goede zorg beschrijven in professionele standaarden.
Argues quality should be a public responsibility with binding rules and enforceable standards rather than voluntary self-regulation, and criticises the lack of enforcement power of the institute.
These members ask why providers are not being obliged to make the quality of their care public.
Deze leden vragen waarom er niet toe wordt overgegaan zorgverleners te verplichten de kwaliteit van hun zorgverlening openbaar te maken.
Supports the goal of ending voluntary self-regulation but worries about bureaucratic explosion, administrative burden and proportionality of information demands.
However enthusiastic the CDA members are about the proposed policy, they fear a bureaucratic explosion resulting from the bill.
Hoe enthousiast de leden van de CDA-fractie ook zijn over het voorgenomen beleid, zij zijn zeer beducht voor een bureaucratische explosie ten gevolge van het wetsvoorstel.
Asks whether political choices about cost-effectiveness are wrongly delegated to the institute and about the Kamer's structural information rights, and requests an evaluation clause.
The SP members ask the government to include an evaluation provision in the law.
De leden van de SP-fractie vragen de regering om een evaluatiebepaling in de wet op te nemen.
Supports the institute but asks for strict separation between quality policy and benefits management, privacy safeguards, and an evaluation clause.
The D66 members attach importance to a strict separation between these two tasks.
De leden van de D66-fractie hechten belang aan een strikte scheiding tussen deze twee taken.
Asks about the criteria for deciding when standard-setting is too slow and the NZi may take over professionals' role, and about independence from the minister and privacy and an evaluation clause.
The NZi receives the power to take over the role of professionals if it takes too long for a guideline to be produced.
Het NZi krijgt de bevoegdheid om de rol van professionals over te nemen als het te lang duurt voordat een richtlijn tot stand komt.

v.summary: The Council of State's advisory division advised that the draft amendment to the Dutch client rights in care act (establishing a quality institute, NIvZ) be drafted more precisely, that the notion of 'quality' be used consistently, and that the client's perspective be removed from the definition of professional standards, along with several other points on regulatory technique and oversight. The minister's reply largely accepts the drafting and terminology remarks and the oversight and enforcement changes, but rejects the advice to drop the client's perspective from the definition.
concerns: The text and explanatory memorandum should be drafted more precisely and overlapping terms reduced to avoid the impression that government becomes responsible for care quality.
Inconsistent quality terminology and the pleonasm 'kwalitatief goede zorg' should be replaced by the single concept of good care as defined in the Wcz.
The client's perspective in the definition of professional standards gives it undue emphasis and should be removed; the government kept it deliberately, clarifying the text instead.
Enforcement of the quality-indicator reporting duty should be regulated in the Wmg framework rather than by cross-referencing sector law, with the relevant Wmg articles included.
The Adviescommissie Kwaliteit's task of making quality-of-care information transparent should be explicitly laid down in the statute.
The explanatory memorandum should explain why the Inspectie voor de Gezondheidszorg would still need to develop its own indicators given the new register.
Requirement of countersignature by the Minister of Interior under the Kaderwet zbo was dropped because the relevant provision was removed.

33315.s: The bill approves, after the fact, three ministerial regulations issued under Article 20 of the Introduction Act for the public bodies Bonaire, Sint Eustatius and Saba, which amended Dutch Antillean-origin statutes. It also makes a small technical amendment to the Education Act BES and sets the title of the act as the Second Approval and Repair Act BES.
33315.j: The memorandum explains that Article 21 of the Introduction Act requires that ministerial regulations under Article 20 be submitted to parliament for approval by law as soon as possible after adoption.
q: Article 21, first paragraph, of the Introduction Act provides that as soon as possible after adoption of a ministerial regulation as mentioned above, a bill approving this regulation must be submitted to the States General.

Artikel 21, eerste lid, van de Invoeringswet bepaalt dat zo spoedig mogelijk na vaststelling van een ministeriële regeling, zoals hierboven genoemd, een voorstel van wet tot goedkeuring van deze regeling bij de Staten-Generaal wordt ingediend.
d: Artikel 20 Invoeringswet openbare lichamen (as cited in memorie)
amending Antillean-origin statutes for BES islands
p: The bill requires parliamentary approval by law of ministerial regulations that amended statutes, restoring a check on executive rule-making that was otherwise absent under Article 20 of the Introduction Act.

33324.s: The bill modernises the rules on construction, management, use and safety of local railways and assigns responsibility for local rail infrastructure to provincial executives (gedeputeerde staten) and metropolitan regions (dagelijks bestuur), with national inspection supervision. It sets safety management, licensing, personnel and enforcement requirements for local rail operators and infrastructure managers.
33324.j: The memorandum justifies decentralised delegation by subsidiarity and the regions' existing transport responsibilities, and justifies central inspection supervision by uniformity and expertise.
q: The main responsibility for the construction and management of local rail infrastructure is placed with the daily boards of the provinces and metropolitan regions.

Het zwaartepunt van de verantwoordelijkheid voor de aanleg en het beheer van de lokale spoorweginfrastructuur wordt in dit wetsvoorstel bij de dagelijkse besturen van de provincies en de plusregio’s belegd.
d: designation of local railways by royal decree
rules on local railways outside EU directive exemptions, may apply directive and statute provisions
delegation of management powers from provinces/metropolitan regions to municipal executives
method and risk norm for tunnel risk analysis
accessibility rules for railway stations and buildings
traffic safety rules on local railways and adjacent roads
accessibility of rolling stock for persons with disabilities
medical examination rules for safety-function staff
professional competence requirements for safety functions
cost recharging and fees for supervision
rules on alcohol and drug testing procedures
p: Provincial executive or metropolitan board may require permits for works near local railways and set the spatial profile, with refusal grounds tied to safety and efficient use.
Prohibits interference with railway installations and obstruction of railway traffic, with limited exceptions for lawful management.
Gives designated officials investigative powers over operators and managers, with executive bodies refraining only where the Dutch Safety Board investigates.
Gives executive bodies power to impose coercive orders and administrative fines up to specified amounts on natural persons and enterprises.
Allows officials to impose driving-style bans and to compel breath and blood testing of persons in safety functions, with ministerial and prosecutorial authority.
Designates the Rotterdam district court as exclusive forum for appeals against decisions under the act, departing from the general venue rule.

parties: Asks how decentralised authorities will avoid each developing their own safety norms and who will coordinate and check alignment of safety management systems of manager and operator.
Who will check whether the safety management systems of manager and operator are actually aligned with each other?
Wie gaat toetsen of de veiligheidszorgsystemen van beheerder en vervoerder daadwerkelijk op elkaar worden afgestemd?

Questions whether the delegation of provincial powers to municipal executives and the spread of responsibilities across provinces and plusregio's make accountability less clear, and asks about state supervision intensity.

Does the government agree that the possibility of delegation, together with the spreading of these powers across provinces and plusregio's, makes the division of responsibilities even less transparent?

Is de regering het met de leden eens dat door deze mogelijkheid van delegatie, en de met dit wetsvoorstel reeds ingezette spreiding van deze bevoegdheden over de provincies en de plusregio’s, de verdeling van verantwoordelijkheden nog onoverzichtelijker wordt?
Asks how the power to delegate to municipal executives fits with a clear allocation of ultimate administrative responsibility, and how much supervision and enforcement costs will be.
Can the government explain the advantages of delegating powers, and how this delegation power fits with the clear demarcation of ultimate administrative responsibility?

Kan de regering toelichten welke voordelen het delegeren van bevoegdheden biedt? En kan de regering daarbij aangeven hoe deze delegatiebevoegdheid past binnen de eenduidige afbakening van bestuurlijke eindverantwoordelijkheid?

Questions the equivalent-safety principle at level crossings and asks for a proportionality principle, and asks why the Onderzoeksraad voor de Veiligheid investigation provision excludes provincial or plusregio's own investigations.
These members ask the government to clarify the regulations on this point so that the proportionality principle carries more weight.
Voornoemde leden vragen de regering om regelgeving op dit punt te verduidelijken, zodat het proportionaliteitsbeginsel zwaarder gaat wegen.

Argues the permit requirement in article 12 should not override the municipality's role as road manager and should allow refusal to ensure efficient use of the road, proposing an amendment to that effect.
That is why the VVD members advocate leaving the final authority with the municipality as road manager, so that one government directs maintenance on urban infrastructure projects.

Daarom pleiten de leden van de VVD-fractie ervoor om de finale bevoegdheid bij de gemeente als wegbeheerder te laten, zodat één overheid de regie voert over het onderhoud op stedelijke infrastructurele projecten.

Asks whether the bill conflicts with the Monasch initiative law on tendering freedom and whether it forces tendering of management, and asks why ILT enforcement powers against the commissioning party are not regulated.
Is it correct that the ILT, unlike in other fields such as main railways, can act independently and also act against the commissioning party, while this bill does not regulate it that way?

Klopt het dat de Inspectie Leefomgeving en Transport (ILT) in tegenstelling tot bij andere velden zoals hoofdspoorwegen wel zelfstandig kan optreden en wel de mogelijkheid heeft om ook op te treden tegen de opdrachtgever terwijl dat in deze wet niet op die manier wordt geregeld?
Has taken note of the bill and has no questions at this time.
The PVV members have taken note of the bill and at this time have no need to ask questions.
De leden van de PVV-fractie hebben kennisgenomen van het wetsvoorstel en hebben op dit moment geen behoefte tot het stellen van vragen.

Asks about the bill's relation to the EU fourth railway package, safeguarding the independence of the infrastructure manager for fair access, and whether freight carriers were involved in advisory body decisions.
These members also ask whether the independence of the infrastructure manager is guaranteed in the interest of fair access for carriers on local railways.
Deze leden vragen tevens of de onafhankelijkheid van de infrastructuurbeheerder gewaarborgd is in het belang van eerlijke toegang voor vervoerders op lokale spoorwegen.
Has taken note of the bill and has no questions at this time.
The 50PLUS members have taken note of the bill and at this time have no need to ask questions.
De leden van de 50PLUS-fractie hebben kennisgenomen van het wetsvoorstel en hebben op dit moment geen behoefte tot het stellen van vragen.

v.summary: The Afdeling advisering of the Raad van State supports the Wet lokaal spoor bill but raises points on the EU rail directive exemption, deviations from the Belemmeringenwet privaatrecht (fixed decision deadline and suspension of the access obligation), and overlapping criminal provisions. The minister's nader rapport accepts most remarks, including dropping the fixed deadline, adding suspension, aligning penalties with the WVW 1994, and removing the duplicate offence.
concerns: The Afdeling asked that the EU rail directive exemption be explained and clarified, and the bill was amended so that a railway is either a main line or a local line, with the designation decree stating the regime.
The fixed twelve-week decision deadline for the Afdeling bestuursrechtspraak in the Belemmeringenwet deviation was objected to as interfering with judicial freedom, and the government removed it.
The Afdeling advised that the access obligation be suspended until the appeal period has expired, which the government adopted.
Lower penalties for refusing breath or blood tests than in the WVW 1994 were questioned, and the government aligned the sanctions with the WVW 1994.
The duplicate criminal offence for damaging local railway infrastructure overlapped with article 351 of the Wetboek van Strafrecht and was removed.
Various redactional comments in the annex on wording, cross-references and numbering were largely adopted, except one on article 35 about maintenance wording.

33351.s: The bill removes the requirements of irreversible infertility and physical sex reassignment for changing the sex entry in a birth certificate. Instead of a court order, the civil registrar would add a later entry of the sex change upon a declaration from a gender-dysphoria expert that the conviction is lasting.
33351.j: The memorandum justifies the change by reduced cost and burden for applicants, the absence of a substantive test by the registrar, and alignment with international recognition practice and Council of Europe and EU human rights standards.
q: The change of the sex entry in the birth certificate can be made directly by the civil registrar; a visit to the court will no longer be necessary for this.

De wijziging van de vermelding van het geslacht in de akte van geboorte zal direct door de ambtenaar van de burgerlijke stand kunnen worden bewerkstelligd, de gang naar de rechter zal daarvoor niet meer nodig zijn.
